items.title: Claude-assisted Lean proof of the Riemann Hypothesis posted by an Anthropic mathematician
items.summary: An Anthropic mathematician reports a Lean-formalized proof of the Riemann Hypothesis (and its generalized form) produced with Claude, with a public archive; early posters say it compiles and the statement matches, but it is a claim awaiting peer review and the dependency on Lean kernel checks is still being examined.

doubt.pushback: Not peer-reviewed; reviewers have checked the target theorem but not every deduction, per replies read.

reception.summary: Replies and search results mostly repeat the claim; a few say the proof compiles across kernels with no obvious exploit tells, others stress it is unreviewed and the Clay prize needs years of scrutiny.

items.title: Gemini 4 Hydrogen scores 92.5% on ARC-AGI-2 in ARC Prize verified testing
items.summary: ARC Prize reports verified scores of 92.5% (ARC-AGI-2, $1.26/task) and 98.5% (ARC-AGI-1) for Google's Gemini 4 Hydrogen, with about 52% fewer reasoning tokens than Gemini 3.8 Flash at high reasoning; the thread also notes API issues (malformed function calls, recitation stops) that blocked full ARC-AGI-3 testing.

items.title: Gemini adds GIF creation using Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash
items.summary: Gemini can now generate looping GIFs from a prompt using its Omni 1.2 Flash video model, available to all Google AI subscribers and free in several countries.

items.title: Zyphra releases MAIA, a team AI colleague, in free beta
items.summary: Zyphra's MAIA is an AI teammate that remembers team decisions, works across Slack, Drive and Confluence, and builds interactive artifacts such as charts and animations; downloadable and free during beta.

items.title: NVIDIA WorldTrace keeps interactive video world models consistent on revisits without retraining
items.summary: NVIDIA Research's WorldTrace helps interactive video world models remember places when the viewer looks away and returns, with results reported on the LoopBench benchmark.

items.title: Real-time image generation in the browser on WebGPU with Jeveration
items.summary: A Qwen 3.5 4B based, single-forward-pass image model with an int8 ONNX checkpoint runs in real time in the browser on WebGPU, shown on an M2 Pro.

items.title: QwenFX runs a stripped-down Vercel fx agent inside Qwen3.5-4B forward passes
items.summary: An open repo that embeds an agent loop in the model's own forward passes so a 4B Qwen can call tools, patch repos and open PRs.

items.title: Diffusers adds LoRA fine-tuning for NVIDIA RFD4-Proteina protein design
items.summary: Hugging Face Diffusers can now LoRA fine-tune NVIDIA's RFD4-Proteina, extending the library to protein design.

items.title: Microsoft previews RDMA over USB4 on Windows for multi-PC local model inference
items.summary: Microsoft's developer preview links several Windows PCs over USB4 for tensor-parallel inference, with RDMA round-trip latency about a quarter of Ethernet on the same cable.

items.title: Hume adds entity accuracy to its ASR leaderboard and releases a training dataset
items.summary: Across 45 ASR systems the best got 81.7% of entities (names, emails, account numbers) exactly right, and two systems with near-identical WER differed by 7 points on entities; Hume published the benchmark and a dataset of these failures.

items.title: Hugging Face reports running its own CDN at about 1 exabyte per month
items.summary: Hugging Face describes building its own CDN for AI downloads, citing roughly 420 GB/s and 80,000 requests/s, with a live traffic visualization.

items.title: GPT 6.2 Astra added to PostTrainBench, Anthropic models still ahead
items.summary: The PostTrainBench team added OpenAI's GPT 6.2 Astra to the benchmark and reports Anthropic models still lead.
